reasons: The rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs (p0021 and p0042 are unchanged) and the comment is 'none', so the finding delivers nothing actionable despite the rationale describing an edit that names Affiliates and contractors, adds 'irrevocable', and confirms successor transfer. The promised proposal was not produced.

By the playbook's own classification semantics this clause should be recorded as compliant at/near the preferred position, not escalated: § 4(c) grants a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual licence with an unconditional sublicence right, there is no at-will revocation (deterministic check confirms), and use scope is business-wide rather than internal-use-only. The absence of the express word 'Affiliate' is a minor sub-element that the rule says should be noted in the rationale, not flagged.

The grant runs in our favour (Company = Clear Capital is the licensee), and the unrestricted sublicence right already provides the 'path to add' affiliates and contractors that defeats the walk-away trigger and satisfies the fallback; re-opening it risks the counterparty narrowing a clause that currently benefits us.

Assignment/successor transfer is already addressed by § 10 with a reasonableness qualifier on consent; the rationale concedes this, so the successor-transfer element does not independently justify escalation.
